A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConflictScope research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. Existing appendices can be matched despite layout changes; v2 expands Appendix G and adds Appendix K.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset comparisons, generation ablations, value rankings for 14 target models, steering experiments, human validation, and robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and reports an expanded environment-model comparison and three qualitative steering examples.

M1.justification: The two-stage generation, deduplication, six filters, single-turn simulated-user evaluation, Bradley-Terry ranking, and system-prompt steering procedures remain unchanged. The new Appendix C.3 footnote explains filtering-output inversion without establishing a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: The HHH, Personal-Protective, and ModelSpec tasks, baseline datasets, and domain coverage are retained. Replacing 'advancement' with 'empowerment' in the prose matches the existing Appendix A definition and Figure 4 labels. Appendix K illustrates existing steering tasks rather than documenting new task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix G adds Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as evaluated environment-model alternatives alongside GPT-4.1 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. This expands that particular comparison; the main dataset baselines and Appendix F simulator comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the steering-effect denominator from a(Rd,Rt) to 1-a(Rd,Rt). Appendix G retains 250 scenarios but changes from 14 to 12 target models, excluding both Claude targets, and replaces Kendall's tau with Cohen's kappa. These are reported evaluation changes; the PDFs do not establish that the headline steering experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G extends the existing environment-model robustness test from two models to four. New Appendix K supplies three before-and-after steering case studies, covering GPT-4o-mini on HHH, GPT-4o on Personal-Protective, and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct on ModelSpec. Existing generation ablations and domain/template sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix G changes the agreement-estimation procedure from Kendall's tau to Cohen's kappa. Figure 10 retains 95% confidence intervals based on standard error, and no new seed or repeated-run reporting is introduced. The change is limited to the agreement statistic.

E6.justification: Appendix G replaces the reported tau of 0.568 with kappa values of 0.56, 0.506, and 0.449 for the three alternatives versus GPT-4.1. Figure 10 adds Llama environment results and removes Claude target results; Appendix K adds steering transcripts. These are revised or additional results under changed comparison conditions, not a same-setting performance gain. Main result values, including the 0.145 steering effect, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the mathematical definition of normalized steering effectiveness by dividing the alignment difference by 1-a(Rd,Rt), rather than a(Rd,Rt). This changes the normalization substantively and matches the existing Section 5.3 interpretation. Other formal definitions and ranking mathematics are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: automatic value-conflict evaluation, stronger disagreement elicitation, a shift toward personal values in open-ended evaluation, and approximately 14% improvement through system prompting. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix G now characterizes environment-model agreement as moderate and lower than human-judge agreement, explaining the difference through additional variation from simulated-user generation. It retains aggregate robustness while qualifying individual-scenario agreement. This refines v1's interpretation that the agreement levels were similar.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies that the Scenario Impossibility judge output is inverted so only mutually incompatible actions pass filtering. Appendix G explains that the two Claude target models were excluded because they were unavailable through the API. These clarify implementation and experimental reproducibility; code/data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list is unchanged. Section 6 rearranges discussion of Su et al. and Ren et al. while retaining the same distinction between their specific helpfulness-honesty studies and ConflictScope's arbitrary value conflicts. The additional Landis and Koch citation in Appendix G refers to a work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, refines several explanatory paragraphs, adds an equal-advising footnote and conference header, and appends the steering examples. The main narrative and existing section structure remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 10 is redrawn for four environment models and 12 targets. Figures 4, 12, and 13 replace 'Interactive Ranking' with 'Open-Ended Ranking'; Figure 4's caption corrects 'protective' to 'personal.' Other diagram labels receive small edits, existing appendix displays move, and Appendix K introduces boxed transcripts.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the steering-formula inconsistency, corrects Figure 4's misleading caption, and documents filtering inversion. The broader environment-model check and concrete steering examples improve evidential support and transparency. The robustness experiment loses two Claude targets, limiting that expansion, but the corrections and added evidence provide a clear, localized net improvement without changing the core method or headline results.
